slot.brief: Hard: simplify/evaluate an expression like a×(b×c) + b×(c×a) or prove a Jacobi-identity style relation; requires careful identity use and possibly given magnitudes/angles.

stem: If $\vec a,\vec b,\vec c$ are unit vectors and $\vec a+\vec b+\vec c=\vec 0$, then $\left|\vec a\times(\vec b\times\vec c)+\vec b\times(\vec c\times\vec a)+2\vec c\times(\vec a\times\vec b)\right|$ equals

verdicts.working: Since |a+b|²=|c|²=1, a·b=−1/2; cyclically, all pairwise dot products are −1/2. The vector inside the norm simplifies by the triple-product identity to −(a−b)/2. As |a−b|=√3, its magnitude is √3/2.

working:
By the cyclic identity, $\vec a\times(\vec b\times\vec c)+\vec b\times(\vec c\times\vec a)+\vec c\times(\vec a\times\vec b)=\vec 0$; the expression reduces to $\vec c\times(\vec a\times\vec b)$. $\vec a\cdot\vec b=-\dfrac12$, so $|\vec a\times\vec b|=\dfrac{\sqrt3}{2}$. Since $\vec c\perp(\vec a\times\vec b)$, the required magnitude is $\dfrac{\sqrt3}{2}$.

Independent check: Since |a+b|²=|c|²=1, a·b=−1/2; cyclically, all pairwise dot products are −1/2. The vector inside the norm simplifies by the triple-product identity to −(a−b)/2. As |a−b|=√3, its magnitude is √3/2.
solution:
Using $\vec x\times(\vec y\times\vec z)=\vec y(\vec x\cdot\vec z)-\vec z(\vec x\cdot\vec y)$, the cyclic sum of the three nested cross products is $\vec 0$. Hence the given vector reduces to $\vec c\times(\vec a\times\vec b)=-\dfrac12(\vec a-\vec b)$, since all pairwise dot products are $-\dfrac12$.
$$\left|\vec c\times(\vec a\times\vec b)\right|=\frac12|\vec a-\vec b|=\frac12\sqrt{2-2\vec a\cdot\vec b}=\frac{\sqrt3}{2}.$$
